title: Weekly Outlook: Fed Hawkishness, Global PMIs,  Micron Earnings and US-China Summit in Focus
intro:
Weekly Outlook: Fed Hawkishness, Global PMIs,
Micron Earnings and US-China Summit in Focus

Wall Street enters the new week facing a delicate balance between resilient economic growth, rising geopolitical risks, and the Federal Reserve’s renewed tightening cycle. Investors will be closely monitoring global PMI surveys, Federal Reserve speakers, the Bank of Japan and Swiss National Bank policy outlooks, the highly anticipated Trump-Xi summit, and Micron Technology earnings as markets search for direction after a volatile week.
The previous week was dominated by the Federal Reserve's first interest rate hike in more than three years, escalating tensions in the Middle East, and a sharp surge in energy prices following attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Although equities recovered late in the week, investors remain cautious as Treasury yields continue to trade near multi-year highs and inflation risks remain elevated.

Market Recap: Fed Hike and Oil Shock Drive Volatility
The Dow Jones Industrial Average recorded its third consecutive weekly decline as investors adjusted to a more hawkish Federal Reserve.
The S&P 500 finished the week mixed, while the Nasdaq Composite managed a modest gain thanks to continued strength in large-cap technology and semiconductor stocks.
Markets were shaken after Chair Kevin Warsh delivered the first rate hike since 2023, raising concerns that inflation may remain elevated longer than previously expected. The Fed also upgraded its inflation and growth forecasts while signaling that additional tightening remains possible before year-end.
At the same time, Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure pushed Brent crude above $104 per barrel and WTI crude near $101, creating a significant geopolitical risk premium across commodity markets.
The combination of higher energy prices and Treasury yields trading around or above 5% has become the primary challenge for risk assets heading into the final week of September.

Federal Reserve Speakers Take Center Stage
Following last week's policy decision, investors will closely monitor comments from Federal Reserve officials throughout the week.
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee is scheduled to speak on Monday, followed by Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams on Tuesday.
Markets will look for confirmation that policymakers remain concerned about inflation risks, particularly those linked to energy prices and continued economic resilience.
Any indication that additional rate hikes remain likely could provide further support for the U.S. dollar while maintaining pressure on equities and longer-duration assets.

Flash PMIs: A Key Test for Global Growth
Wednesday's release of September Flash PMI data will likely be one of the week's most important economic events.
Investors will receive early readings from:
United States
Eurozone
United Kingdom
The surveys will provide fresh insight into economic activity, business confidence, employment trends, and inflation pressures.
Particular attention will be paid to the price components of the reports following recent producer price data that suggested inflationary pressures remain persistent.
Stronger-than-expected PMIs would reinforce the narrative of economic resilience but could also strengthen expectations for further monetary tightening. Conversely, weaker data could support hopes that inflation will moderate without additional policy action.

US-China Summit Could Shape Risk Sentiment
One of the most significant geopolitical events of the week will be Thursday's meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Trade policy, tariffs, rare-earth exports, technology restrictions, and artificial intelligence are expected to dominate discussions.
Investors will be watching for signs that both nations are willing to maintain or expand their existing trade truce.
A constructive outcome could improve global risk sentiment, benefiting cyclical sectors, industrial companies, semiconductor stocks, and commodity-linked currencies such as the Australian and New Zealand dollars.
Any renewed tensions could quickly reverse recent market optimism and increase volatility across global equity markets.

Central Banks Remain in Focus
Bank of Japan
The Bank of Japan recently raised interest rates to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995, highlighting growing concerns about inflation and rising energy costs.
Investors will continue assessing whether Japanese policymakers may need to tighten further if inflation pressures persist.
Swiss National Bank
The Swiss National Bank announces its policy decision on Thursday.
Markets broadly expect rates to remain unchanged at 0.0%, as Swiss inflation remains relatively subdued compared with other developed economies.
Attention will focus on updated inflation forecasts and any comments regarding potential intervention in currency markets should the Swiss franc strengthen excessively.

Energy Markets Remain a Major Risk Factor
Crude oil remains one of the most important variables for global markets.
Although prices eased late last week as Saudi Arabia worked to restore flows through its East-West pipeline, geopolitical tensions remain elevated.
Any additional disruptions to Middle Eastern energy infrastructure could quickly push oil prices higher again, potentially reigniting inflation fears and placing upward pressure on bond yields.
Investors should continue monitoring developments involving Saudi Arabia, Iran, and regional security conditions throughout the week.

Gold and the US Dollar
Gold remains highly sensitive to movements in Treasury yields and oil prices.
After rebounding toward $4,350 per ounce, the precious metal could continue finding support if yields retreat or geopolitical risks intensify.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index remains near multi-week highs following the Fed's hawkish shift. Strong economic data and expectations for additional tightening could continue supporting the greenback against major currencies.

Earnings Spotlight: Micron Technology
The most important corporate event of the week will be Micron Technology's earnings report.
The semiconductor company has become a critical gauge of AI-related demand and memory-chip market conditions.
Investors will focus on:
AI-driven demand trends.
Data center spending.
High-bandwidth memory (HBM) demand.
Revenue guidance.
Capital expenditure plans.
Commentary on enterprise and cloud spending.
Given Micron's position within the AI supply chain, its results could influence sentiment across the broader semiconductor sector, including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and other AI-related names.
A strong report could reinforce confidence in the AI investment cycle, while weaker guidance may revive concerns about slowing growth and elevated valuations across the technology sector.

Economic Calendar Highlights
Monday
Chicago Fed National Activity Index
Speech from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee
Tuesday
Speeches from Philip Jefferson and John Williams
Wednesday
US Flash PMI
Eurozone Flash PMI
UK Flash PMI
Weekly Jobless Claims
Thursday
Trump-Xi Summit
Swiss National Bank Policy Decision
Micron Technology Earnings
Friday
Atlanta Fed GDPNow Update
Additional Federal Reserve commentary

Market Outlook
The week ahead could prove pivotal for both equity and commodity markets.
Investors will need to navigate a combination of hawkish central bank signals, elevated geopolitical risks, critical PMI data, and major developments in U.S.-China relations.
The Federal Reserve's renewed tightening cycle has shifted the market narrative from rate cuts back toward inflation control, placing greater importance on incoming economic data.
Meanwhile, oil prices, Treasury yields, and AI-related earnings will remain the key drivers of market sentiment.
For now, the broader trend remains constructive for risk assets, but volatility is likely to remain elevated as investors assess whether strong growth can coexist with higher interest rates and persistent geopolitical uncertainty.
